implementation_notes: The native form: the compiler generates the state machine from the promise type, and the three-function awaiter protocol lets the fast path avoid suspending. Use symmetric transfer (await_suspend returning a coroutine_handle) so a chain of awaits runs in constant stack.
idiom_name: co_await / co_yield with a promise_type and std::coroutine_handle
pitfalls: void await_suspend grows the stack per completion.
The frame is heap-allocated unless it does not escape.

variants.name: Boost.Coroutine2 (stackful)
variants.idiom_name: boost::coroutines2::coroutine<T> with an allocator for the stack
variants.implementation_notes: The pre-C++20 and stackful alternative: each coroutine owns a real stack (so it can suspend at any call depth with no colouring), at the cost of stack memory per instance and a dependence on a Boost version.
pitfalls: Resuming from a different thread needs care with thread-local state.
A Boost dependency for what C++20 now provides in the standard.
